Round 2 · Implementation · Hard

Ticket #06 — Warehouse Shipment Processing

Difficulty: Hard

Context

You maintain a warehouse's shipment service. A SKU is an identifier for one stock item, such as sku-a. Stock on hand is the quantity physically in the warehouse. Reserved units are held for orders and are still on hand but cannot be promised again. Available units equal on-hand minus reserved units.

fulfill(order_id, lines, allow_partial=False) receives a mapping from SKU to requested quantity. All-or-nothing means every requested unit ships or none ships. Partial fulfillment ships available units; a backorder records the requested units that could not ship.

Practice report

Start with no reservations and stock sku-a=4, sku-b=2. Call fulfill("o1", {"sku-a": 3, "sku-b": 3}) in that line order.

Point in the request sku-a sku-b
On hand before the request 4 2
Reserved before the request 0 0
Requested, all-or-nothing 3 3
Current starter after returning backordered 4 on hand; 3 reserved 2 on hand; 0 reserved
Expected after the failed attempt 4 on hand; 0 reserved 2 on hand; 0 reserved

The unsuccessful order must not leave those 3 sku-a units unavailable to the next order. On a fresh copy of the same stock, allowing partial fulfillment instead should ship 3 sku-a and 2 sku-b, leave on-hand quantities 1 and 0, and record a backorder of 1 sku-b.

Acceptance Criteria

  • An all-or-nothing order ships every line or leaves on-hand quantities and reservations as they were before the attempt. Its backorder covers the unshipped request.
  • Existing reservations reduce availability and must survive another order's failed attempt. Reserved stock never exceeds on-hand stock.
  • A failed attempt leaves no reservation created by that attempt behind.
  • With partial fulfillment enabled, ship only available units and record each unshipped remainder. Shipped plus backordered units equal requested units.
  • Retrying a shipped or partially shipped order returns already_shipped without deducting stock again.
  • Reject empty requests and invalid quantities before stock changes. Quantities must satisfy the existing positive-integer contract; zero, negative, and non-integer quantities are rejected.

Out of Scope

Keep the supplied repository and recorded backorders. Purchasing replacement stock, automatically retrying backorders, shipping-carrier APIs, and database concurrency are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce both modes from separate fresh repositories. Trace the service and warehouse records, then prove the stock and reservation invariants with tests for a shortage on a later line, pre-existing reservations, invalid quantities, and completed-order retries. Explain the state before and after each request.
